When RELOAD = 0 and the number of data bytes defined in NBYTES[7:0] is transferred: • In automatic end mode (AUTOEND = 1), a STOP condition is automatically sent. • In software end mode (AUTOEND = 0), the TC flag is set and the SCL line is stretched low, to perform software actions:

A RESTART condition can be requested by setting the START bit of the I2C_CR2 register with the proper target address configuration and the number of bytes to transfer. Setting the START bit clears the TC flag and sends the START condition on the bus.
A STOP condition can be requested by setting the STOP bit of the I2C_CR2 register. This clears the TC flag and sends a STOP condition on the bus.
When RELOAD = 0 and he number of data bytes defined in NBYTES[7:0] is transferred: • In automatic end mode (AUTOEND = 1), a NACK and a STOP are automatically sent after the last received byte.

Firmware then sets START (a repeated START: clears TC, sends the START and address; for a write-then-read, the read follows with no STOP between) or STOP (clears TC, sends a STOP; STOPF is set when that STOP is detected). For a read, a NACK is sent after the last received byte, then TC is set.
silicon.1: Automatic end mode: when NBYTES are transferred a STOP is sent automatically (for a read, after a NACK of the last byte); STOPF is set at that STOP; TC is not set (TC needs AUTOEND = 0).

twin.0_write: At the TXDR write that makes NBYTES bytes, the stock model hands the device all of them (Write), then SetTransferCompleteFlags: TC = 1, TXIS = 0, no STOPF, no FinishTransmission, controller mode kept (masterMode stays true). The guard's Open() sees TC at the next access and closes the open transfer, so a following START is not refused (L578); the stock START clears TC and starts the next transfer at once, with no FinishTransmission between: silicon's flag sequence (TC, then the firmware's own START, TC cleared, then TXIS or RXNE of the new phase).
twin.0_stop: A STOP written after TC: the guard passes it (controller is still true) and closes the transfer; the stock StopTransfer sets STOPF, calls FinishTransmission and leaves controller mode, but does not clear TC: TC stays 1 until the next START (L340) or PE = 0, and with TCIE = 1 the event line stays asserted (L461).
twin.0_read: The stock START reads all NBYTES from the device into its queue at once; TC is set only by the RXDR read that empties the queue (L385-388), not when the last byte arrives.
twin.1: At the completing TXDR write (or the RXDR read that empties the queue), STOPF = 1, the device's FinishTransmission, controller mode left, TC not set: silicon's flags. The guard closes the transfer on that STOPF, unless STOPF was already 1 at the START (staleStopf, L306, L642-643): then neither TC nor a new STOPF edge closes it, and the next START is refused as "START while a transfer is open".

differs: (a) Value 0, then STOP (ArduPilot's path at every transaction end): silicon clears TC when STOP is set (p2011, p1975); the twin keeps TC = 1 after the STOP, with STOPF = 1, until the next START or PE = 0, and with TCIE = 1 the I2C event interrupt stays asserted. (b) Value 0, read transfer: silicon sets TC when NBYTES have been received (p2011, p1979); the twin sets it only at the RXDR read of the last byte (RM0433 does not say in words whether silicon's TC waits for that read; p2011 ties it to the transfer). (c) Value 1 with a STOPF left uncleared before the START: the guard never closes the transfer, so the firmware's next START is refused (TVI-I2C-TRANSFER; dropped in enforcing mode) where silicon starts it. (d) Time only, both values: every completion (TC or STOP/STOPF) is immediate at the access that completes NBYTES; no SCL stretch or bus time. The repeated START asked about (value 0, write then read) is not a difference: the twin gives TC, then the firmware's START clears TC, with no STOPF and no STOP between.

silicon.0x0: The reset value, which RM0433 requires these bits to keep: no effect.
silicon.0x2: Not stated: RM0433 says only "Reserved, must be kept at reset value".

twin.all: The guard passes bits 2:1 to the stock ICR unchanged (it looks only at NACKCF and STOPCF, and strips NACKCF). The stock register has no field at bits 2:0 (a RESERVED tag), so no value is stored and no callback runs; a non-zero value is only logged ("Unhandled write"). No register, flag or interrupt changes, for 0x0, 0x2, 0x4 and 0x6 alike.

differs: Not established for 0x2 and 0x4 (and 0x6): RM0433 states no behaviour for a non-reset value in ICR bits 2:1, so silicon's effect cannot be read; the twin changes nothing. For 0x0, same (nothing happens on either side).
observable_by_firmware: none that the manual lets be shown: the twin changes no register, flag or interrupt; whether silicon does anything is undocumented. A log line in the twin is not visible to firmware.
notes: ChibiOS writes ICR = 0x2, 0x4 or 0x40 at every ICR write it makes (TVI-WO-1306.measure.md L107; bit 6 is the separate row I2C_ICR.Res6); these are the TXIS, RXNE and TC positions of ISR, none of which an ICR write clears on silicon (TXIS clears at a TXDR write, RXNE at an RXDR read, TC at START or STOP, p2011). That ArduPilot works on silicon with these writes is evidence that silicon ignores them, but it is not a reading. One row covers i2c1-i2c3.

rm.quote: Bits 7:0 TXDATA[7:0]: 8-bit transmit data Data byte to be transmitted to the I²C-bus Note: These bits can be written only when TXE = 1.
In the case of a write transfer, the TXIS flag is set after each byte transmission, after the ninth SCL pulse when an ACK is received.
The flag is cleared when the I2C_TXDR register is written with the next data byte to transmit.
The number of TXIS events during the transfer corresponds to the value programmed in NBYTES[7:0].

Bit 1 TXIS: Transmit interrupt status (transmitters) This bit is set by hardware when the I2C_TXDR register is empty and the data to be transmitted must be written in the I2C_TXDR register. It is cleared when the next data to be sent is written in the I2C_TXDR register.

Bit 0 TXE: Transmit data register empty (transmitters) This bit is set by hardware when the I2C_TXDR register is empty. It is cleared when the next data to be sent is written in the I2C_TXDR register.

If the I2C_TXDR register is not empty (TXE = 0), its content is copied into the shift register after the ninth SCL pulse (the acknowledge pulse). Then the shift register content is shifted out on the SDA line.

silicon.all: The byte written is the next data byte to send: copied to the shift register after the ninth SCL pulse of the previous byte and shifted out on SDA; TXE and TXIS clear at the write, and TXIS is set again after that byte's ACK (NBYTES TXIS events in all); a write is allowed only when TXE = 1.

twin.all: With PE = 1 and an open write transfer (START passed, RD_WRN = 0, NBYTES not yet sent), the guard passes the word (bits 31:8 must be 0); the stock model queues (byte)value and, when the queue holds NBYTES bytes, hands the device all of them in one Write and completes (TC or STOPF per AUTOEND). TXIS reads 1 from the START until that last write; TXE always reads 1. The byte values reach the device unchanged.

differs: Flags and time only; the bytes the device receives, and their order, are the same for every value. (1) After a TXDR write that is not the last, TXIS and TXE read 1 at once (silicon: both 0 until the byte has moved to the shift register and, for TXIS, been ACKed). (2) A TXDR write while TXE = 0, which silicon does not allow, is accepted. (3) The device gets the NBYTES bytes in one Write at the last one, with no bus time.
observable_by_firmware: ISR.TXIS (bit 1) and ISR.TXE (bit 0) read right after a TXDR write; the elapsed time of a write transfer. A firmware that waits for TXIS before each write (as both measured firmwares poll ISR) sends the same bytes in the same order.
notes: Writes outside a write transfer's data phase (PE = 0, no START, a read, or NBYTES already sent) are refused by TVI-I2C-TRANSFER before stock sees them. The stock TXDR defines bits 7:0 and reserves 31:9 (L302-303), leaving bit 8 undefined; the guard's Reserved 31:8 row (Zero) refuses any write with bit 8 set. A TXDR read returns the stock field's stored value (rw on p2014). One row covers i2c1-i2c3.

rm.quote: Bits 31:0 TXDR[31:0]: transmit data register The register serves as an interface with TxFIFO. A write to it accesses TxFIFO.
Note: DR can be accessed byte-wise (8-bit access): in this case only one data-byte is written by single access.

When the data frame size fits into one byte (less than or equal to 8 bits), the data packing is used automatically when any read or write 16-bit or 32-bit access is performed on the SPI_RXDR/SPI_TXDR register.
Bit 1 TXP: Tx-packet space available 0: there is not enough space to locate next data packet at TxFIFO 1: TxFIFO has enough free location to host 1 data packet
Bit 0 RXP: Rx-packet available 0: RxFIFO is empty or a not complete data packet is received 1: RxFIFO contains at least 1 data packet
Bit 3 EOT: end of transfer EOT is set by hardware as soon as a full transfer is complete, that is when TSIZE number of data have been transmitted and/or received on the SPI.
In SPI mode, the bit is taken into account at master mode only. If transmission is enabled, communication starts or continues only if any data is available in the transmission FIFO.

silicon.all: An 8-bit write puts one data byte (one 8-bit frame) into TxFIFO; the master sends it on the bus when SPE = 1 and CSTART = 1, at the SPI clock; TXP shows whether TxFIFO has space for another packet, RXP when a received frame is in RxFIFO, EOT when TSIZE frames are done. (A 16- or 32-bit write would pack 2 or 4 frames: not passed by the guard.)

twin.all: The guard passes only an 8-bit TXDR write (frame 8 bits), with SPE = 1; the stock model queues the value and, with SPE and CSTART set, at once sends its low byte to the device (Transmit), puts the reply in the RxFIFO and counts the frame; EOT (with FinishTransmission and CSTART cleared) when TSIZE frames are done. TXP always reads 1. The byte values reach the device unchanged, MSB-first ordering being moot for one byte.

differs: FIFO occupancy and time only; the byte sent and the byte received back are the same for every value. (1) Each frame is exchanged at the write (with CSTART set), so RXP, EOT and TXC are set immediately, with no bus time. (2) TXP never reads 0: the twin's TxFIFO has no capacity limit (silicon's depth is not quoted here), so a firmware writing ahead of the bus, or before CSTART, is never held off.
observable_by_firmware: SPI_SR.TXP (bit 1) never 0; SPI_SR.RXP (bit 0), EOT (bit 3) and TXC read set right after the write; the elapsed time of a transfer (and of a DMA stream to TXDR).
notes: 16- and 32-bit TXDR writes (silicon's packing, p2178) are refused by TVI-SPI-WIDTH, and a TXDR write with SPE = 0 by TVI-SPI-ORDER, so only byte writes of byte frames reach the stock model; a byte write goes to the stock WriteByte, which calls the stock WriteDoubleWord with the byte zero-extended (L53-56), and with DSIZE = 7 byteCount is 1, so GetBytesFromValue takes the low byte. DSIZE must be 00111 at the enable (guard TVI-SPI-FIELD) and LSBFRST is Zero only, so frame size and bit order match silicon's at every write that passes. spi1 and spi2 are the same class and path. TXDR is write-only (p2227); a read is refused (TVI-SPI-READ).
